SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
Cashier
The Cashier automatically takes at most one payment per turn, from the customer who has been ready to pay the longest.
Chef
The Chef completes one preparation unit of one order per turn.
ComboMeal
A combo made of two existing menu items.
ConsoleInput
Reads the manager's choices from the keyboard, or from a script file redirected into the program.
ConsoleView
Prints the game state to the console.
CriticCustomer
A food critic.
Customer
A restaurant customer.
CustomerStatus
The stages a customer moves through during a visit.
DemoJump
Saved points in the game that we can jump to during the demo in the pixel-art window.
Dish
A single dish with a fixed price and preparation time, such as a Salad.
Game
Handles the game rules for each turn.
GameController
Runs the turn loop.
GameResult
The outcome of a finished game.
GameStats
Running totals used for the end-of-turn summary and the final result.
HappyHour
Happy Hour: a promotion the manager may switch on once per game, at the start of a turn.
Host
The Host greets customers and seats at most one queued customer per turn, in addition to whatever the Waiter does.
InvalidActionException
Thrown when the manager chooses an action that the game rules do not allow, for example seating a customer at an occupied table.
Main
Starts Restaurant Rush.
Menu
The list of menu items customers can choose from.
MenuItem
Something a customer can order.
Money
An immutable, non-negative amount of money stored as whole cents.
Objective
The targets the manager must reach by the final turn.
Order
One customer's order.
OrderStatus
The stages an order moves through.
PixelGame
The pixel-art window.
PixelGame.Action
 
PixelGame.Phase
 
PixelRoom
Paints the dining room from the current game state.
PixelRoom.Stop
 
PixelRoom.Walker
A sprite follows queued waypoints in screen space.
PriceCalculator
Calculates the price a customer pays for an item when the order is taken.
PriceModifier
A pricing rule for the whole restaurant, such as Happy Hour.
RegularCustomer
An ordinary customer: loses 8 satisfaction per waiting turn and pays full price.
Restaurant
The restaurant floor: the menu, the tables, the waiting queue, every customer who has arrived and every order taken.
Scenario
The base setting from the brief: 18 turns, 2 tables, the three-dish menu and one arrival on turns 1, 4, 7, 10, 13 and 16.
Staff
A staff member who can complete at most one task per turn.
Table
A dining table that holds at most one customer.
VIPCustomer
A VIP customer: more patient (loses 5 satisfaction per waiting turn) and gets 10% off the bill.
Waiter
The Waiter seats customers, takes orders and serves READY dishes, one task per turn.
